The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ff3098c8faf29685), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 33-34. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Let (Ω, g, k) be a smooth polarized one-ended exterior, complete with its compact nonempty boundary included. Assume the boundary is strictly future trapped, k has compact support, g − δ = Oj(r−1) for every finite j, Rg = O(r−3−δ) for some 0 < δ < 1, and g has finite ADM energy. Let m > 0 be a smooth invariant function such that m ≤ 8π(µ − |Jcon|g), inf C m > 0 for every compact C ⊂ Ω, m ≥ cr−3−δ on the end for some c > 0. There is an invariant reduced exterior Ωred ⊂ Ω, obtained by removing full trapped regions and retaining the component toward infinity, with smooth nonempty compact boundary, for which the following holds. For every sufficiently small fixed ε > 0, and all sufficiently large integers n along a sequence, there are smooth invariant functions fn, tn and positive smooth profiles ln(t) such that ḡn = g + ln(tn)2 df2 n, ĝn = e4tn ḡn, wn = ln(tn)∇fn q 1 + ln(tn)2|dfn|2 g , tn ≥ −ε, (6.3) 1 2 e4tn Rĝn ≥ 8π µ + Jcon(wn)  − m 2 . (6.4) 33 The inner boundary has strictly negative mean curvature in ĝn for its normal toward infinity. The metric ĝn is complete with boundary, is asymptotically flat of order one with at least two controlled derivatives, and has finite energy satisfying Eĝn ≤ Eg + on(1). (6.5) Here the reduced domain and its collars are fixed before ε and n. For each fixed n the functions are obtained by exhaustion of finite outer truncations; the error in Equation (6.5) tends to zero as n → ∞ after that exhaustion, with the prepared data and ε fixed.
